chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadah, from 'Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who intends to pray eight rak'at but prays ten rak'at: Does he count the two extra rak'at as part of his prayer? He said: 'No, unless he prays them intentionally; if he did not intend that, then no.'

key_terms.يَحْتَسِبُ: To count or consider as part of

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone prays more rak'at than intended by mistake?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the principle of intention (niyyah) in rectifying prayer errors, distinguishing between accidental excess and deliberate addition. It underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis that validity often hinges on conscious intent rather than mere physical action, a key distinction in the science of *al-Sahw* (forgetfulness). This ruling provides practical guidance for worshippers to ensure their prayers are accepted by maintaining precise alignment between their internal purpose and external performance.
